rows.label: The token 'nerve' itself, in Latin-script languages (nerve, nerves, Nerven, Nerv, nerfs), whatever the sense
The nerve / nervous-system concept across languages, strongest for Arabic عصب
Pain: the word and the concept (pain relief, painkillers, chronic pain)
The nervous system and neuroanatomy: nerves, brain regions, motor control

Incoherent; best guess: mundane concrete/technical tokens (code variable names like data/conf, product/licence nouns, capitalized name fragments like Camp, Standard, IS) in non-supernatural contexts, the opposite of the ghost/spirit + pole
Final subword/token completing a proper name (person, river, city, regnal numeral, initial) or a header/sign-off delimiter in encyclopedic, reference-list and crossword-style text
Words marking a return/resumption to a previous state or activity after an interruption (again, returns, resume, back in, return to, settle back)
The token 'vic'/'Vic'/'VIC' in any form: Victoria state abbreviation, Vicente, vicar, vicarious, Roman inscription VIC
Animals named or described in casual/narrative text: animal names (rhino, ape, crab, chickens, chimera) and their sounds/behaviours (hissing, croaks), not sensory physiology
Final digit(s) of a p-value in reported statistics (P = 0.03_, p=.01_), typically biomedical abstracts
The word 'disappointed' (especially 'won't be disappointed' / 'will be disappointed')
Place/person names containing the 'any' subword, above all 'Albany' (also Thanyaburi, Sukanya), in addresses and citations
References to Christianity, Christians, Jesus/Yeshua or Messianic belief, especially in texts about Jews and Judaism
Cognitive-psychology/neuroscience-of-memory terms: episodic (incl. Russian эпизод-), encoding/coding, PET, GABA, beta amyloid, experiment components
Nouns/modifiers marking an exemplary, leading or showcase role: flagship, pilot (projet pilote), phare, statement piece, indicator species
Weak: inner/final piece of named entities and alphanumeric designations (Anzac, AIM-120, ADAM-12, Nature Conservancy, Arts Center, deaminase)
Bibliographic reference text: journal titles, publishers, society names, DOIs/URLs inside citations
Incoherent; best guess: the 'CAS' acronym plus mid-word fragments in Russian (по-яс) and Arabic (عص/ب, as in عصبي, عصا)
Rare Latinate technical descriptive terms (often split subwords) in botanical/anatomical/medical descriptions: vestiture, sequelae, pendulous, exfoliative, assemblage, border

Incoherent; best guess: content tokens in factual/statistical reporting prose, especially epidemiology and clinical statistics (odds ratio, p-value digits, disease names like diarrhea, citation dates), as opposed to Python import names

Biology/physiology/chemistry textbook tokens that are not cell-type names: heredity traits, elements and minerals (zinc, arsenic), anatomical structures (geniculate body, peripheral parts), tissue descriptions, incl. Russian medical text
Software/online service plan or license tiers: free vs paid version, subscription, trial/evaluation, upgrade to Plus/Premium, Standard/Advanced editions
The token 'motor' (esp. 'electric motor', 'induction motor', 'DC motor', and Motor in names like Motorcycles)
Word-initial 'p'/'P' token, especially the single-letter variable p at the start of a code line (p = Parser(), p.select) and initial P of proper words split off (Pole, Pfund)
The spelling 'diarr' (diarrhea/diarrhoea/diarrea in English and Spanish) and the look-alike Malian surname Diarra

Early Christian / Jewish history and preaching context: words like Jews, Judaism, non-Jews, Tabernacle, Roman-world cultures, sermon/reformer names (not academic theology terms like theological, exegetical)
'of' inside titles of books/films/shows ('The Haunting of Hill House', 'The Adventures of Tintin'), plus letter sign-off punctuation ('Thanks,' 'Regards,')
The token 'trait'/'traits' (personality traits, genetic traits, Python traits library, also French 'traité')

Neuroscience research on brain circuitry: hippocampal subregions (CA3), brain anatomy (reticular formation, geniculate body, efferent tracts), neural coding (sparse, rate code), neuroscientist names (LeDoux, Panksepp)
Eager anticipation: 'can't wait', 'can hardly wait', 'impatient', French 'avoir hâte'/'avec impatience'
Subword continuation inside place-names beginning Tul-/Tuil-/Nur- (Tulare, tularemia, Tuileries, Nuremberg)

Describing a task or situation as emotionally overwhelming or stressful for the person (overwhelming, nerve-wracking, unbearable, 'can't handle', 'a tricky task'), as opposed to neutral technical difficulty (challenging, difficult)
'B'/'bb' token inside all-caps acronyms or code identifiers with doubled B (SSB, DBB, Aabb, ABB'), not B in personal names like Bob/Bobbie
Pain words in non-English languages, at the word-internal token: German Schmerz(en), Spanish doler/duele, Arabic وجع/مؤلم, Russian боли

Mostly incoherent: mid-sentence CJK tokens (Chinese, some Japanese) in narrative or commentary prose, often the word that completes an evaluative or emotional predicate (失望, 失落/有些, 陋习, 完善); best guess is a general Chinese-prose continuation feature

Desktop PC software UI and Windows-era program names: completions like right-click, Windows Live, Shockwave Player, Norton Commander, vcruntime, and the same in other languages (правой кнопкой мыши, 右クリック)

Python code: a dotted reference to a module, class or object attribute used as a value, especially on the right of an assignment or after if/elif (logger.error, sys.stdout.write, settings.DEBUG, logging.getLogger, self._flag)
The word 'motor' / 'Motor' (and the 'otor' piece of non-motor, sensory-motor): motor skills, motor symptoms, Ford Motor Company, motor museum/yacht
Tomato(es) and pastes (tomato paste, shrimp paste, coarse paste) as ingredients in recipe instructions or ingredient lists; not pepper/salt seasonings
The preposition token ' on' in running English text (on a platform, on a day, on the side, compliment on, on Earth)
Sufism: the 'uf' piece of Sufi/Sufis (Islamic mystics), with some spillover to South Asian religious ritual terms (mehendi)
English 'Ab'-initial word pieces: the place name Albany (city, prison, orogen) and 'aberr-' (aberrant, aberration); not French ab- words like abord/abandonne
The suffix '-ate' completing Latinate, often anatomical or technical words (striate, geniculate, cingulate, fastigiate, implicate, associate, Kongregate)
Autonomic/nervous-system stimulation physiology word pieces: parasympathetic, muscarinic, vagal, excitation, overstimulating, irritants (раздражители); not drug names
Colloquial discourse markers, interjections and expressive punctuation in informal speech or chatty prose (you know, well, Ну, Aaaah, '!', '?', '…and')
Suspense and close watching: 'closely watched', 'watched closely', 'keep in suspense', 'nail-biter', German 'gespannt'
The verb 'serve'/'serves' (especially 'serve as', serving visitors or guests)
Arabic word-final 'ب' piece (and 'بة/بات') completing words like واجب (duty), وجبة/وجبات (meal/s), صاحب
